feature: Released Photonz can use the microphone
summary: The downloaded app is now signed with the microphone entitlement, so the first recording with sound shows macOS's microphone prompt and Photonz appears under Privacy & Security > Microphone. Every release build and every CI build now fails if the entitlement goes missing.
setup: The next released Photonz (needs a patch release; this fix is not in v0.17.0), on a Mac where Photonz has never asked for the microphone. No flag changed from its default.

try.do: Install the new release from its DMG and launch it.
Start a screen recording with a microphone picked in the audio menu.
Confirm macOS asks whether Photonz may use the microphone, and click Allow.
Stop the recording and play it back: your voice is in it.
Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone and find Photonz listed and on.
Turn Photonz off there, record again, and click Open System Settings in the sheet: it lands on the Microphone list with Photonz in it.

evaluate: Does the microphone prompt appear on the first recording with sound, in front of everything else?
Is Photonz in the Microphone list afterwards, on your other machine as well?
When the microphone is off, does the sheet's Open System Settings land on the Microphone list rather than somewhere else?
rough: Not checked on a notarized build yet: there is no Developer ID certificate on this Mac, so it can only be checked once a release is cut. The local proof is a small test app signed with the same hardened runtime: without the entitlement macOS answered 'denied' at once, with no prompt and no entry in the Microphone list; with it, macOS held the request on a 260 by 218 prompt window until it was dismissed.
No screenshots: this Mac's terminal has no Screen Recording grant, and the fix changes signing only, not anything on screen.
Notarization accepting the entitlement is expected (it is a standard one) but is only proven when the next release's notarize step goes green.

Hardened runtime audit: the app loads no third-party libraries, uses no Apple Events, no JIT and no camera, and on-device speech transcription and screen capture need no entitlement, so the microphone is the only one added.
